topics.label: Introduction to cancer causes and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture and states its objectives before the substantive material begins.

topics.label: Cancer as mutation-driven clonal evolution in a permissive microenvironment
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain cancer as an evolving population of mutated cells and introduce the endogenous, environmental, inherited, and cellular factors that can drive that evolution.

topics.label: Environmental cancer risks and their interpretation
topics.groupedBecause: Together these subtopics examine how environmental exposures relate to cancer risk and how chance, inherited susceptibility, and population patterns complicate interpretation.

topics.label: Infectious agents in cancer development, with Burkitt lymphoma as an example
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how infections can contribute to cancer and explain the interacting roles of EBV, malaria, and MYC translocation in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Environmental carcinogens and mechanisms of DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how dietary and environmental exposures can damage DNA directly or after metabolic activation, producing mutations associated with cancer.

topics.label: Tumour promotion and context-dependent susceptibility to carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show that cancer development depends not only on DNA damage but also on promotion and on biological context, including developmental stage and tissue.

topics.label: Human evidence for carcinogen exposure and cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe how mutation patterns and population-based studies can help identify carcinogen exposures and assess their links to cancer.

topics.label: Experimental tests of carcinogenicity and their limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe laboratory approaches for testing carcinogenic potential and explain why animal and bacterial assays cannot fully represent cancer development in humans.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This final subtopic recaps the lecture’s conclusions and closes by emphasizing the choices involved in weighing cancer risks against benefits.
